qAndA.answer: The client wanted both dust and sand to be visible in the sand falling effect, requiring the team to carefully balance the two elements.
qAndA.question: What specific challenge did Nofeel and his team face while creating the sand falling effect in Star Trek Prodigy?

qAndA.answer: They gathered references, brainstormed, and created test animations that they shared with the client for approval before proceeding with the rest of the shots.
qAndA.question: How did Nofeel and his team ensure that the client's vision for the sand falling effect was achieved?

qAndA.answer: He saw it as a way to express his passion for art and to showcase his work to future generations.
qAndA.question: What was Nofeel's initial motivation for choosing a career in animation?

qAndA.answer: He says it was a 'great sensation' and that he was 'speechless' seeing the combined efforts of the entire team come together.
qAndA.question: How does Nofeel describe the feeling of seeing the final output of the Star Trek Prodigy project?

qAndA.answer: He mentions being a fan of sci-fi movies and series, and considers Star Trek to be one of the best, making it a 'souvenir' for him to work on this project.
qAndA.question: What special significance does Star Trek hold for Nofeel?

text_to_speech: I'm Novefel, I'm FX supervisor on Star Trek: Prodigy. Presently I have a 16 year experience in  the animation field. I saw animation as an opportunity,   as an exciting way to  show my passion for the art field and a place where I   can show the future generations my work.   I felt I could do by selecting this industry. I joined Mikros Animation in 2012 so it's been almost 10 years in Mikros Animation. I had worked on many projects like "Barbie in the Pink Shoes", "How to train your dragon", "The adventures of Puss in Boots", "Adventures in Wonder Park" (TV series),  "Rugrats" (reboot) and presently for Star Trek: Prodigy. Presently our team is consisting of 10 people - we have one lead artist and three seniors and four mid-level and one junior. I'd be having discussions with the Nickelodeon client, and we'd brainstorm what needs  to be done, what they would all expect. Arts and references are shared from the Nickelodeon client, And then we'd do our "homework", looking for what other references are needed. We'd collect them and share   with the team. Then we'd ask them like "How it is achievable?" "How it can be done?" To me, the best part in FX was the sand falling which should have dust and sand both together. So we had created it with a lot of care, and we  showed it to the Nickelodeon creatives. They were happy with the result, and they told us to add it in all of the remaining shots. It was a really a good sensation, a great feeling - like what we are showing, they are appreciating it and it is also looking good! It's really a great experience to see our first images coming out really good because the whole team has been working from different locations and like we are combining together, and seeing a final awesome output. That specific moment was when we saw the final shots   in a sequence combining the efforts of the whole  team. That's not only FX, there are also rigging, animation, texturing, lighting, compositing ... Everything had come out really good and we were really   like speechless after seeing the output. Working on Star Trek : Prodigy is kind   of a souvenir on its own for us. As CG FX persons, we used to watch a lot of sci-fi movies and series   and all and Star Trek is one of the best. So it was a great pleasure working on it!
